issues.display_title: Issue #4395: feat(auth): read the SSO switch from the API instead of a build setting
issues.main_description_html:
Background

#4388 added an on/off switch for Single Sign-On (SSO) login, but the switch is a build setting (REACT_APP_KEYCLOAK_AUTH_ENABLED). Every change needs a rebuild and deploy, and the dev and live dashboards can't be switched separately. This task makes the switch from #4388 outdated: the switch now comes from the API (GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#2074).

Goal

Each time the dashboard loads, it asks the API whether SSO is on. SSO can then be switched on or off without a rebuild, separately for dev and live.

Scope

  • When the dashboard loads, it asks the API for the switch and says which environment it is: localhost and dev.gothru.co count as dev, everything else as live.
  • Login page:
    • While the switch is loading, a loading screen shows (never the login form).
    • SSO on: users go straight to the SSO login page, as in #4388.
    • SSO off: the normal login form shows, as today.
    • If the switch can't be loaded (API error, no connection, or no answer within 5 seconds), users see "Can't load sign-in options" with a "Try Again" button. Neither the login form nor SSO is shown. Try Again asks once per click; nothing retries on its own.
  • Logout goes to the SSO login page only when the switch has loaded and is on. Otherwise it goes to the login page, which loads the switch again.
  • The REACT_APP_KEYCLOAK_AUTH_ENABLED build setting is removed.

Out of Scope

  • Updating the fallback login from #4392 (PR #4393) to use the new switch. That is aligned after this task.
  • Maintenance mode stays a build setting.
  • Changing the switch itself (done in Redis; see the API task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: With the switch on for this environment, the login page goes straight to the SSO login page and the login form never appears.
  • AC-002: With the switch off, the login page shows the normal login form, as today.
  • AC-003: localhost and dev.gothru.co follow the dev switch; the live dashboard follows the live switch.
  • AC-004: While the switch is loading, the login page shows a loading screen, not the login form.
  • AC-005: If the switch can't be loaded, users see "Can't load sign-in options" with Try Again. The page doesn't reload on its own or show repeated pop-ups, and Try Again loads the switch once.
  • AC-006: Logout goes to the SSO login page when the switch is on, and to the login page otherwise.
  • AC-007: Changing the switch in Redis takes effect on the next page load, without a rebuild.
  • AC-008: Unit tests cover AC-001 – AC-007.

Dependencies

  • GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#2074: the feature-flags API

Related

  • #4388: SSO switch as a build setting (outdated by this task)
  • #4389: PR for #4388
  • #4392 / #4393: fallback login, to be aligned to this switch afterwards

Result

Implementation

  • PR: #4396 — merged into development on 2026-10-16 (merge commit 19bbf06)
  • Key commit: 40128ca — feat(auth): read Keycloak SSO switch from feature-flags API instead of env
  • Behavior:
    • On each page load the dashboard asks GET /v1/feature-flags (GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#2074) for the SSO switch. localhost and dev.gothru.co use the dev switch; everything else uses the live switch.
    • Login page: a loading screen while the switch loads; straight to SSO when it is on; the normal login form when it is off.
    • If the switch can't be loaded (API error, no connection, or no answer within 5 seconds), users see "Can't load sign-in options" with a "Try Again" button. Try Again asks once per click; nothing retries on its own.
    • Logout goes to the SSO login page only when the switch is loaded and on; otherwise to the login page.
    • The REACT_APP_KEYCLOAK_AUTH_ENABLED build setting is no longer used and can be removed from the env.
  • To turn SSO on or off: SET feature_flags:<dev|live>:keycloak_auth 1 (on) or 0 (off) in Redis. It takes effect on the next page load, no rebuild needed.

Testing

  • CI=true npx craco test --watchAll=false src/hooks/useFeatureFlags src/utils/featureFlagEnv src/reducers/featureFlags src/pages/Auth src/components/Header src/App.test.jsx → 9 suites, 52/52 passed (AC-008)
    • Switch per environment: localhost / dev.gothru.co → dev, other hosts → live (AC-003)
    • Loading → loading screen, no form and no redirect (AC-004)
    • Switch on → straight to SSO; switch off → normal login form (AC-001, AC-002)
    • Switch can't be loaded → "Can't load sign-in options" + Try Again, no automatic retry, Try Again asks once (AC-005)
    • Logout → SSO login when on, login page when off or not loaded (AC-006)
  • Full suite: the 8 suites (27 tests) that fail also fail on development without this change.

issues.display_title: Issue #4334: PayPal Buy-Storage: align path with SUBSCRIBE (SSE status stream)
issues.main_description_html:
Context

PayPal Buy-Storage (space addon) currently uses client-driven capture (capturePaypalSubscription via /paypal/subscriptions/capture).
We need to align the Buy-Storage flow with the SUBSCRIBE, UPGRADE, and DOWNGRADE webhook-first patterns.

Goal

Bypass the capture endpoint call from the browser for BUY-STORAGE, listening instead to the real-time SSE subscription status stream until completion.

Frontend Checklist

  • In src/components/organism/PaymentV2/PaymentV2.jsx:
    • Add isBuyStorage guard (plan?.action?.toUpperCase() === 'BUY-STORAGE' && !oneTimePaymentSubscription) to bypass capturePaypalSubscription.
    • Route BUY-STORAGE to listenSubscriptionStatus (SSE stream /paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/status-stream).
    • Confirm success handler (onPaymentFinalSuccess -> handleSpaceAddonSuccess) triggers profile and storage quota refresh on active SSE status.
    • Handle timeout and failure events gracefully via existing error/timeout patterns.
  • Unit testing:
    • Add test coverage in src/components/organism/PaymentV2/PaymentV2.countly.test.jsx verifying that BUY-STORAGE routes to SSE without calling the capture endpoint.

Acceptance Criteria

  • No capture request is dispatched from the browser on PayPal buy-storage approval.
  • The UI listens to the SSE status stream and shows the success modal / refreshes storage quota upon webhook completion.
  • Unit tests pass 100%.

issues.display_title: Issue #4332: PayPal Downgrade: align path with SUBSCRIBE (SSE status stream)
issues.main_description_html:
Context & Problem Statement

Previously, PayPal subscription downgrades dispatched a synchronous HTTP request to POST /paypal/subscriptions/capture upon user approval in the PayPal modal. To eliminate data loss caused by unexpected browser closures and align with the backend's webhook-first architecture, the frontend must bypass client-side capture for downgrades and listen to real-time status updates via Server-Sent Events (SSE).

Related Backend Issue: GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#1951

Scope of Work & Acceptance Criteria

  • Bypass Synchronous Capture (PaymentV2.jsx):
    • Update handlePaypalSubscriptionApprove to exclude DOWNGRADE actions from the capturePaypalSubscription call.
    • Normalize action string comparisons using .toUpperCase() across all branches (SUBSCRIBE, UPGRADE, DOWNGRADE) to avoid casing mismatches.
  • Integrate Real-Time SSE Status Stream:
    • Route DOWNGRADE actions into listenSubscriptionStatus (via usePaypalSubscriptionStatus hook listening to /paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/status-stream).
    • On active status: Dismiss the loading spinner, invoke handleDowngradeOrUpgradeSuccess() without a page reload, and show downgrade success confirmation.
    • On failed status: Surface appropriate error messages and trigger onPaymentFinalError().
  • UX & Telemetry Handling:
    • Handle stream timeouts (45s heartbeat): display an informative toast (t_paypal_timeout_processing) explaining that the change is processing in the background, then dismiss modal gracefully.
    • Track Countly analytics properly (subscription_changed or subscription_change_failed).
    • Suppress purchase receipt / invoice popups since downgrades involve no immediate charge.

Result

    • src/components/organism/PaymentV2/PaymentV2.countly.test.jsx: Added unit tests verifying SSE stream listening, graceful timeout handling, and verified onPurchaseCompleted is excluded on downgrade.

Testing Results

issues.display_title: Issue #4347: fix(navigation): enable native middle-click new tab and link behavior across dashboard
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Middle-clicking (mouse wheel click / auxiliary click) on navigation items and links throughout app.gothru.co currently fails to open links in a new tab. Previously, a partial workaround was implemented in commit 125344b77 (PR #2270) that hardcoded onMouseDown (e.button === 1) exclusively for /my-tours across side menu files.

This issue aims to systematically resolve navigation link semantics across the entire dashboard so that middle-click, Ctrl+click, Cmd+click, and "Open link in new tab" work natively as expected.

Root Cause

  1. Missing href attributes on NextUI components: NextUI components such as ListboxItem, DropdownItem, and BreadcrumbItem only render semantic HTML <a> tags when provided an href prop. When omitted and driven solely by onPress={() => navigate(...)}, they render as <li>, <button>, or <span>, preventing browsers from recognizing them as links.
  2. Relative path and click interception in tour listings: In TourCard.jsx and ToursTable.jsx, href is defined without a leading slash (my-tours/...), causing invalid relative URL resolution on new tab opens. Furthermore, openTourDetail in List.jsx executes event.preventDefault() unconditionally.
  3. Non-semantic header links: The logo in Header.jsx uses href="javascript:;", opening broken/blank pages on middle-click.

Scope of Changes & Acceptance Criteria

  • Side Menus (MainMenu, AdvanceMenu, TourMenu, PhotographerNoviceMenu, PhotographerMenu, ProfileMenu, SupportMenu):
    • Add appropriate href props to all navigation ListboxItem components.
    • Remove hardcoded onMouseDown (e.button === 1 / window.open('/my-tours', '_blank')) workarounds.
  • Tour Listing (TourCard.jsx, ToursTable.jsx, List.jsx):
    • Fix relative href paths to absolute dynamic paths (/my-tours/${item.moderation_id} or /upload based on tour wizard/panoramas).
    • Ensure middle-click (e.button === 1) and modifier clicks (metaKey, ctrlKey) do not have their default browser behavior prevented.
    • Suppress href in selection mode so middle-click does not navigate while selecting tours.
  • Header & Breadcrumbs (Header.jsx, PageLayout.jsx):
    • Replace href="javascript:;" on the header logo with a valid route /.
    • Provide href props for BreadcrumbItem and DropdownItem navigation elements.
  • Verification:
    • Middle-click opens links in a new background tab natively.
    • Left-click maintains client-side SPA navigation via React Router without full page reloads and respects IsBlockingNavigate.
    • All existing unit tests pass.
